+import json
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+
+
+df = duckdb.sql(
+    """
+    SELECT EXTRACT(year FROM crash_date)::INTEGER AS year,
+           SUM(number_of_pedestrians_killed)::BIGINT AS pedestrians_killed
+    FROM read_parquet('data/crashes.parquet')
+    WHERE crash_date >= DATE '2013-01-01'
+      AND crash_date < DATE '2026-01-01'
+    GROUP BY year
+    ORDER BY year
+    """

+df.to_csv("out/values_1.csv", index=False)

+ax.set_ylabel("Pedestrians killed (count)")
+ax.set_ylim(0, max(df["pedestrians_killed"]) * 1.15)
+ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.22)
+ax.set_axisbelow(True)
+fig.tight_layout()
+fig.savefig("out/option_1.png", dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
+plt.close(fig)
+
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual sum of pedestrians killed",
+            "denominator": "Not applicable; raw annual count",
+            "grouping": "Crash year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Bar chart",
+            "reason": "Annual counts directly answer how many pedestrians were killed each year and make year-to-year differences easy to compare.",
